references.text: The original institution of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, where Israel was commanded to eat unleavened bread for seven days as a permanent statute.
Moses exhorts the people to remember this day when they went out of Egypt and repeats the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days in the month of Abib.
A parallel command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib, which marks the time of the Exodus from Egypt.
The Law's reiteration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread as one of the Lord's feasts, with specific instructions for the seven days.
Regulations concerning the feast to be held on the fourteenth day of the first month, followed by seven days of unleavened bread.
Moses repeats the command regarding Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, referencing the month of Abib and the Exodus from Egypt.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread is mentioned as one of the three annual pilgrimage feasts when all men were to appear before the Lord.
Jesus and his disciples prepare the Passover meal on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, fulfilling the Old Testament feast.
Paul uses the symbolism of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, describing Christ as our Passover lamb, and urges believers to keep the feast with unleavened bread.
Complementary explanation: The source verse specifies the timing, while this verse explains the symbolism behind 'the bread of affliction' and the haste of the Exodus.
Confirms the same historical event and emphasizes the feast's status as a permanent ordinance for all generations.
